original_value: The term cyber physical systems (CPS) refers to a new generation of systems with integrated computational and physical capabilities through computation, communication, and control. In the past decades, related techniques for CPS have been well studied and developed, and are widely applied in the fields such as industrial automation, smart transportation, aerospace, environment monitoring, and smart grids. However, with the expansion of CPS complexity and the enhancement of the system openness, most of CPS become not only safety‐critical but also security‐critical since deeply involving both physical objects and computer networks. In the last decade, it is no longer rare to see safety incidents and security attacks happening in industries. Safety and security issues are increasingly converging on CPS, leading to new situations in which these two closely interdependent issues should now be considered together, rather than separately or in sequence. This paper reviews the existing approaches of risk assessment and management from the perspective of safety, security, and their integration. The comparisons of these approaches are summarised with their pros and cons before the technical gaps between the demand and the current situation of safety and security issues in CPS are identified.

result.paraphrase: Cyber physical systems (CPS) are a new class of systems that integrate computational and physical capabilities via computation, communication, and control. Over the past few decades, CPS-related techniques have been extensively studied, developed, and widely used in areas such as industrial automation, smart transportation, aerospace, environmental monitoring, and smart grids. As CPS grow more complex and more open, most of them have become not only safety-critical but also security-critical, because they deeply involve both physical objects and computer networks. In the last decade, safety incidents and security attacks have increasingly appeared in industry. Safety and security concerns are converging in CPS, creating new situations in which these closely interdependent issues must be addressed together rather than separately or in sequence. This paper reviews existing risk assessment and management approaches from the viewpoints of safety, security, and their integration. It summarizes and compares these approaches, outlining their advantages and disadvantages before identifying the technical gaps between the current state and the requirements of safety and security issues in CPS.
